title: Kyoto Bar Lets Disabled People Work via Robot
paragraphs: In Japan, a snack bar isn't a place you go to for a quick bite. It's a small bar where customers come not only for drinks, but also to talk. They usually sit at a counter, while the owner — often a woman known as "Mama" — serves drinks and chats with everyone.
Now, a new snack bar in Kyoto is giving Mama's job to robots — but there will still be a real person behind every conversation.

OrySnack Kyoto, which will open on December 4, will use robot bartenders controlled remotely by human "pilots." Many of the pilots have disabilities or illnesses that make it difficult for them to leave home. Through the robots, they will be able to serve drinks and talk to customers without actually being there.

The Kyoto bar is the latest project from OryLab, the company behind Avatar Robot Cafe Dawn in Tokyo. That cafe opened in 2021, and now has more than 100 pilots working remotely, with around 5,000 customers visiting each month.
In August this year, OryLab already opened an OrySnack bar inside its Tokyo cafe. Unlike the main cafe, the snack bar puts more focus on conversation and connecting with customers.
The Kyoto bar will have nine seats and some standing space where customers will be able to try different kinds of sake along with snacks.
OryLab was founded by inventor Kentaro Yoshifuji, who became interested in remote robots after illness kept him out of school when he was young.

So, while robot bartenders certainly sound cool, the real idea is to give more people the chance to work, meet others and build connections. OryLab hopes that one day, some pilots may even be able to run snack bars of their own.
